ei.subject: 수능특강Light 영어
ei.title: The whole morning had been chaotic.

fullPassage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.

questions.passage: The whole morning had been (A)[organized / chaotic]. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with (B)[limited / endless] security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the (C)[handful / crowds] of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 혼돈 상태인(chaotic), 끝없는(endless), 군중(crowds).
det.analysis:
✅ ① chaotic — endless — crowds: 아침이 '혼란스러웠고', '끝없는' 보안 검색줄을 마주했으며, 사람들의 '무리'를 헤치고 갔다는 문맥에 모두 적합합니다.
❌ ② organized — endless — crowds: organized(정돈된)는 혼란스러운 아침과 반대입니다.
❌ ③ chaotic — limited — crowds: limited(제한된)는 끝없이 이어지는 보안줄과 반대입니다.
❌ ④ chaotic — endless — handful: handful(소수)은 인파를 헤치고 달려간 상황과 맞지 않습니다.
det.tip: chaotic ↔ organized, endless ↔ limited, crowds ↔ handful

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an (A)[mild / intense] rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an (B)[advertisement / announcement] saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at (C)[tension / ease]. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 극심한(intense), 안내 방송(announcement), 편안한(at ease).
det.analysis:
✅ ② intense — announcement — ease: 자명종이 안 울려 '극심한' 서두름에 빠졌고, 비행기 지연 '안내 방송'을 듣고, 마침내 '편안함'을 느꼈다는 문맥에 적합합니다.
❌ ① mild — announcement — ease: mild(가벼운)는 자명종이 안 울린 상황의 긴박함과 맞지 않습니다.
❌ ③ intense — advertisement — ease: advertisement(광고)는 비행기 지연을 알리는 방송이 아닙니다.
❌ ④ intense — announcement — tension: tension(긴장)은 안도감을 느낀 상황과 반대입니다.
det.tip: intense ↔ mild, announcement ↔ advertisement, at ease ↔ at tension

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept (A)[staring at / glancing at] her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an (B)[predictable / unexpected] hour to (C)[waste / spare], she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 힐끗 보다(glancing at), 예상치 못한(unexpected), 할애하다(spare).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ glancing at — unexpected — spare: Sophie가 시계를 '힐끗' 보았고, '예상치 못한' 여유 시간에 상점을 둘러볼 수 있게 되었다는 문맥에 적합합니다.
❌ ① staring at — unexpected — spare: staring at(노려보다)은 초조하게 시계를 '힐끗힐끗' 보는 상황과 다릅니다.
❌ ② glancing at — predictable — spare: predictable(예측 가능한)은 '예상치 못한' 여유와 반대입니다.
❌ ④ glancing at — unexpected — waste: waste(낭비하다)는 여유 시간이 '생겨서' 쓸 수 있다는 문맥과 다릅니다.
det.tip: glance at = 힐끗 보다 (↔ stare at), unexpected ↔ predictable, spare ↔ waste

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After ①<u>terrible</u> traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with ②<u>endless</u> security lines. Sophie kept ③<u>glancing</u> at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ④<u>anxiety</u>. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ anxiety(불안) → ease(편안함). 깊은 한숨을 내쉬며 마침내 '편안함'을 느꼈다는 문맥이므로 anxiety는 부적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① terrible: 끔찍한 교통 체증 — 문맥 적절
✅ ② endless: 끝없는 보안줄 — 문맥 적절
✅ ③ glancing: 힐끗 보다 — 문맥 적절
❌ ④ anxiety: 불안 → ease(편안함)이 원문. 한숨을 내쉬며 안도한 상황이므로 anxiety는 반대 의미입니다.
det.tip: at ease(편안한) ↔ anxiety(불안). feel at ease = 마음이 편안해지다

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the ①<u>crowds</u> of people. Just then, she heard an ②<u>announcement</u> saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to ③<u>relax</u> and ④<u>overlook</u> the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ overlook(간과하다) → browse(둘러보다). 여유 시간에 공항 상점을 '둘러본다'는 문맥이므로 overlook은 부적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① crowds: 인파 — 사람들 사이를 헤치며 지나간다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② announcement: 안내 방송 — 비행기 지연 방송이므로 적절
✅ ③ relax: 긴장을 풀다 — 여유 시간에 쉴 수 있다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ overlook: 간과하다/내려다보다 → browse(둘러보다)가 원문. 상점을 '간과하다'는 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: browse = (가게 등을) 둘러보다 ↔ overlook = 간과하다, 내려다보다

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock ①<u>failing</u> to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless ②<u>security</u> lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "③<u>expedited</u>." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ④<u>ease</u>. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ expedited(촉진된) → delayed(지연된). 비행기가 '지연되었다'는 안내 방송을 들었다는 문맥이므로 expedited는 부적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① failing: 작동하지 않다 — 알람이 울리지 않았다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② security: 보안 — 보안 검색줄이라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ expedited: 촉진된/앞당겨진 → delayed(지연된)가 원문. Sophie가 서두르던 상황에서 비행기가 앞당겨졌다면 더 급박해지므로 안도할 수 없음.
✅ ④ ease: 편안함 — 한숨을 내쉬며 안도했다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: delay(지연시키다) ↔ expedite(촉진하다, 앞당기다). delayed가 원문입니다.

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the ____ in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 탑승구(boarding gate). 시간 내에 '탑승구'에 도착할 수 없을까 걱정하며 인파를 헤치고 달려갔다는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② boarding gate: 비행기를 타기 위한 탑승구로, 공항에서 시간에 쫓기는 상황에 가장 적절합니다.
❌ ① ticket counter: 티켓 카운터는 이미 탑승권을 가지고 있는 상황에서 적절하지 않습니다.
❌ ③ baggage claim: 수하물 찾는 곳은 도착 후 이용하는 곳입니다.
❌ ④ parking lot: 주차장은 비행기 탑승과 관련이 없습니다.
det.tip: boarding gate = 탑승구. 공항에서 비행기를 타기 위해 가는 곳.

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ____. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 편안함(ease). 비행기가 지연되었다는 방송을 듣고 깊은 한숨을 내쉬며 마침내 '편안함'을 느꼈다는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ ease: 비행기 지연으로 시간 여유가 생겨 안도하며 편안해졌다는 문맥에 적합합니다.
❌ ① risk: 위험 — 안도한 상황과 반대입니다.
❌ ② fault: 잘못 — 문맥과 무관합니다.
❌ ④ stake: 위태로움 — 긴장이 풀린 상황과 맞지 않습니다.
det.tip: feel at ease = 마음이 편안해지다. ease = 편안함, 안도

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and ____ the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 둘러보다(browse). 예상치 못한 여유 시간이 생겨 공항 상점을 '둘러볼' 수 있게 되었다는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ browse: 가게를 둘러보다 — 여유 시간에 relax와 함께 상점을 '구경하다'는 의미로 적합합니다.
❌ ① abandon: 버리다 — 상점을 버린다는 것은 문맥상 부자연스럽습니다.
❌ ② avoid: 피하다 — 여유 시간에 상점을 피할 이유가 없습니다.
❌ ③ construct: 건설하다 — 상점을 건설한다는 것은 문맥과 전혀 맞지 않습니다.
det.tip: browse = (가게 등을) 둘러보다, 훑어보다. 동의어: look around, scan

questions.passage: The whole morning had been <u>chaotic</u>. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 chaotic과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: chaotic = 혼돈 상태인, 무질서한. disorderly = 무질서한.
det.analysis:
✅ ① disorderly: 무질서한 — chaotic과 동의어입니다.
❌ ② peaceful: 평화로운 — chaotic의 반의어입니다.
❌ ③ systematic: 체계적인 — chaotic과 반대 의미입니다.
❌ ④ ordinary: 평범한 — chaotic과 관련 없습니다.
det.tip: chaotic = disorderly = messy = confused ↔ organized = orderly

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an <u>intense</u> rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 intense와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: intense = 극심한, 강렬한. severe = 극심한, 심한.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ severe: 극심한 — intense와 동의어로, 강도가 높다는 의미입니다.
❌ ① gentle: 부드러운 — intense의 반의어입니다.
❌ ② brief: 짧은 — 강도와 무관한 시간 개념입니다.
❌ ④ gradual: 점진적인 — 갑작스럽고 강렬한 것과 반대입니다.
det.tip: intense = severe = strong = powerful ↔ mild = gentle

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to <u>spare</u>, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 spare와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: spare = (시간을) 할애하다, 내어 주다. afford = 여유가 있다, 할애하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② afford: '여유가 있다'라는 의미로 spare와 유사합니다. 'an hour to spare'는 '여유 있는 한 시간'입니다.
❌ ① spend: 쓰다 — spare는 '남는 시간'의 뉘앙스이지 '소비하다'가 아닙니다.
❌ ③ save: 절약하다 — spare와 비슷해 보이지만, 여기서 spare는 '여분의'라는 의미입니다.
❌ ④ waste: 낭비하다 — spare와 반대 뉘앙스입니다.
det.tip: spare = 할애하다, 내어 주다 / 여분의. time to spare = 여유 시간. 동의어: afford

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with <u>endless</u> security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 endless와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: endless = 끝없는. limited = 제한된, 한정된.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ limited: 제한된 — endless(끝없는)의 반의어입니다.
❌ ① continuous: 계속되는 — endless와 유사한 의미입니다.
❌ ② permanent: 영구적인 — endless와 유사한 뉘앙스입니다.
❌ ③ lengthy: 긴 — endless와 비슷한 방향의 의미입니다.
det.tip: endless = 끝없는 (= infinite, countless) ↔ limited = finite = bounded

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "<u>delayed</u>." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 delayed와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: delayed = 지연된. expedited = 촉진된, 앞당겨진.
det.analysis:
✅ ② expedited: 촉진된, 앞당겨진 — delayed(지연된)의 정확한 반의어입니다.
❌ ① canceled: 취소된 — 지연과 다른 개념입니다. 반의어가 아닙니다.
❌ ③ announced: 발표된 — 지연과 관련 없는 행위입니다.
❌ ④ scheduled: 예정된 — 반의어라기보다 다른 의미입니다.
det.tip: delay(지연시키다) ↔ expedite(촉진하다, 앞당기다). 동의어: postpone, put off

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept <u>glancing</u> at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 glancing/glance의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 힐끗 보다 (B) 대충 훑어보다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 힐끗 보다 — (B) 대충 훑어보다: (A)에서 glancing at은 시계를 '힐끗' 보는 행위이고, (B)에서 glance through는 잡지를 '대충 훑어보는' 행위입니다.
❌ ① (A) 힐끗 보다 — (B) 주의 깊게 읽다: glance through는 '대충 훑어보다'이지 주의 깊게 읽는 것이 아닙니다.
❌ ② (A) 노려보다 — (B) 대충 훑어보다: glancing at은 '노려보다(stare)'가 아니라 '힐끗 보다'입니다.
❌ ④ (A) 노려보다 — (B) 주의 깊게 읽다: 둘 다 glance의 의미와 맞지 않습니다.
det.tip: glance at = 힐끗 보다, glance through/over = 대충 훑어보다. ↔ stare at = 노려보다, gaze at = 응시하다

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a public or formal statement giving information about something"

det.korean: announcement = 발표, 공지. 어떤 것에 대한 정보를 알리는 공식적인 진술.
det.analysis:
✅ ① announcement: '어떤 것에 대한 정보를 알리는 공식적 진술'에 정확히 해당합니다.
❌ ② advertisement: 광고 — 상품 홍보이지 정보 전달이 아닙니다.
❌ ③ argument: 논쟁 — 정보 전달과 무관합니다.
❌ ④ arrangement: 준비, 배열 — 공식 진술과 다릅니다.
det.tip: announcement = 발표, 공지 = statement, declaration. 비슷한 형태에 주의: announcement vs. advertisement

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an __________ (intense) rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport.
questions.stem:
괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.
[intense]

det.korean: intense(극심한). 명사 rush를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 원형 그대로 intense가 정답입니다.
det.analysis: intense는 이미 형용사이고, 명사 rush 앞에서 형용사로 쓰이므로 원형 그대로 사용합니다. intensely(부사), intensity(명사)로 변환하면 문맥에 맞지 않습니다.
det.tip: intense(형용사: 극심한) — intensely(부사: 극심하게) — intensity(명사: 강도). 명사 앞에는 형용사!

questions.passage: Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." With an __________ (expect) hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops.
questions.stem:
괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.
[expect]

det.korean: unexpected(예상치 못한). 명사 hour를 수식하는 형용사 자리이며, 문맥상 '예상치 못한' 여유 시간이 생긴 것이므로 부정 접두사 un-을 붙여야 합니다.
det.analysis: expect(동사) → expected(형용사: 예상된) → unexpected(형용사: 예상치 못한). 비행기가 지연되어 '예상치 못하게' 여유 시간이 생긴 상황이므로 un- 접두사가 필요합니다.
det.tip: expect → expected ↔ unexpected. un- 접두사 = 부정. 비슷한 패턴: usual → unusual, fortunate → unfortunate

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second ____. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: feeling like an hour(한 시간처럼 느껴지는). 매 초가 한 시간처럼 느껴졌다는 표현으로, Sophie의 초조함을 나타냅니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② feeling like an hour: 매 초가 '한 시간처럼 느껴진다'는 표현으로, 시간이 느리게 가는 느낌의 초조함을 잘 드러냅니다.
❌ ① passing by quickly: 빠르게 지나간다 — 초조한 상황에서 시간이 빨리 간다고 느끼는 것은 문맥과 반대입니다.
❌ ③ standing completely still: 완전히 멈춘 — 과장된 표현이지만 원문과 다릅니다.
❌ ④ flying past her: 눈앞을 스쳐 지나가는 — 시간이 빨리 간다는 의미로 문맥과 반대입니다.
det.tip: each second feeling like an hour = 1초가 1시간처럼 느껴지다 → 극도로 초조한 상태를 표현하는 과장법

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." ____, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Letting out a deep sigh(깊은 한숨을 내쉬며). 비행기 지연 소식을 듣고 안도하며 깊은 한숨을 내쉰다는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Letting out a deep sigh: 깊은 한숨을 내쉬며 — 긴장이 풀리고 안도하는 자연스러운 반응으로, 뒤에 'finally felt at ease'와 연결됩니다.
❌ ② Clenching her fists tightly: 주먹을 꽉 쥐며 — 분노나 긴장의 표현으로, 안도와 맞지 않습니다.
❌ ③ Raising her voice in anger: 화를 내며 목소리를 높이며 — at ease와 완전히 반대입니다.
❌ ④ Holding her breath nervously: 긴장하며 숨을 참으며 — 안도감과 반대입니다.
det.tip: let out a deep sigh = 깊은 한숨을 내쉬다 → 안도, 긴장 해소의 표현. let out = ~을 내보내다
